newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMI chief - Maastricht allows deviation from goals.
newsitem.headline: EMI chief - Maastricht allows deviation from goals.

text.p: European Monetary Institute (EMI) President Alexandre Lamfalussy said on Tuesday that the Maastricht Treaty accepted a deviation from the reference levels for budget deficit and government debt that was carefully worded but not quantified.
Lamfalussy said that adherence to the criteria had three elements and that all these three had to be used in assessing which EU members qualify for Europe's planned monetary union.

Firstly the Treaty set reference levels of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) for the budget deficit and 60 percent of GDP for public debt, Lamfalussy told a news conference to mark the launch of the European Central Bank forerunner's third annual report.
Secondly, the Treaty accepted a deviation from the levels and thirdly it insisted on sustainability, Lamfalussy said.
"One has to use all three elements at the same time," Lamfalussy said, adding that was not an easy task.
